newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's TFM says to halve railway labor force.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's TFM says to halve railway labor force.

text.p: Mexican railroad operators Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana (TFM) plan to start operations on Tuesday with about half the workers previously employed on the Northeast railroad, TFM executive vice-president Brad Skinner said.
The formerly government-run railway, considered to have been bloated with extra workers, is the first of three routes to be privatized in a bid to modernize operations.

To this end, TFM cut about half of the railroad's work force. The railway's workers, about 8,500 in 1995, were laid off when the route was privatized and TFM plans to hire back between 3,600 to 4,000 workers, Skinner said in an interview with Reuters late Monday.
The joint venture between Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) and Kansas City Southern Industries made a final payment to the government on Monday to begin operations on Tuesday.
"The government and everyone knew that to be efficient we would need to cut jobs," Skinner said.
Analysts had estimated TFM would only hire about half of the previous employees on the railway. The government paid all
severance and accrued pensions for laid-off workers, he added.
In a labor accord reached last month, TFM promoted the concept of "universal worker," a less specialized worker that can fill various positions.
"It allows more flexibility, for people to be cross-trained. It also allows us to contract out work where needed and be more efficient," Skinner said.
Workers at central railway city San Luis Potosi were cut to 750 from 2,500 in recent government cuts, and efficiency improved 200 percent, Skinner said.
